extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, peer reviewers, and researchers
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of COPE guidance documents and best-practice statements covering editorial management, peer review, authorship disputes, retractions, consent for case reports, text recycling, and cooperation with institutions on misconduct. Intended to guide journals, editors, reviewers and publishers in ethical publication practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for managing the relationships between society-owned journals, their society, and publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: The journals of ‘Learned Societies’ and ‘Professional Associations’ are an important part of the scientific literature. Regardless of the publication arrangements (i.e., self-published by the society, published under contract with a professional publishing house, or some combination of both) and the number of journals affiliated with that society, the policies of and the relationships among the…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Journal management. Action: Download PDF. Guidance addresses policies and relationships between societies, their journals, and external publishers; governance and management considerations for society-owned journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Transparency and Best Practice in Scholarly Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction — The Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE), the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ), the Open Access Scholarly Publishers Association (OASPA), and the World Association of Medical Editors (WAME) are scholarly o…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories: Ethical oversight; Journal management. Versions: View web version; Version 3 (this version), January 2018; Poster version, January 2018. Provides a set of transparency and best-practice standards for publishers and journals (e.g., editorial policies, ownership, peer review processes, fees, copyright and licensing practices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals’ Best Practices for Ensuring Consent for Publishing Medical Case Reports: guidance from COPE
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on ensuring consent for publishing medical case reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories: Ethical oversight; Intellectual property. Action: Download PDF. Sets best-practice standards for obtaining and documenting patient consent for case reports, including what constitutes adequate consent and considerations for anonymization and identifiable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of Information Among Editors-in-Chief Regarding Possible Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: These guidelines have been issued following a COPE Discussion Forum (4 September 2013) and Discussion Document (February 2014) on the subject, and it was initiated in the wake of a number of high-profile cases of research misconduct in which the sharing of inf…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories: Allegations of misconduct; Complaints and appeals; Conflicts of interest / Competing interests; Ethical oversight. Action: Download PDF. Guidance covers when and how editors-in-chief may share information about suspected misconduct with other editors and institutions, confidentiality limits, and appropriate procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text recycling guidelines for editors
rubrics_metrics.description: A common issue encountered by editors is overlap of text with an author’s own previously published work, particularly with the increasing use of plagiarism detection software. This practice is known as ‘text recycling’ (also sometimes referred to as ‘self-plagiarism’). Opinions on the acceptability of text recycling vary greatly and it can be a challenge for editors to know how to deal with it…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Intellectual property. Action: Download PDF. Provides editors with criteria and examples for distinguishing acceptable reuse (e.g., methods) from problematic text recycling, recommended policies to adopt, and suggested author communications and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Short Guide to Ethical Editing for New Editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised by Tara Hoke, Originally written by Margaret Rees — Becoming an editor of a journal is an exciting but daunting task especially if you are working alone without day to day contact with editorial colleagues. This short guide aims to summarise key issues and to provide links to relevant pages of the COPE website as well as those of other organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories: Ethical oversight; Journal management. Action: Download PDF. Practical guidance for new editors on key ethical issues, editorial responsibilities, decision-making, and where to find further COPE resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Editors: Research, Audit and Service Evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for editors on handling submissions that are research, audit or service evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Journal management. Action: Download PDF (PDF, 107 KB. Version 2, January 2014). Offers criteria to help editors distinguish between research requiring ethics approval and audits/service evaluations, and how to assess and report such manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: COPE Ethical Guidelines for Peer Reviewers - English
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review in all its forms plays an important role in ensuring the integrity of the scholarly record. The process depends to a large extent on trust, and requires that everyone involved behaves responsibly and ethically. Peer reviewers play…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Peer review processes. Action: Download PDF. Sets expectations and standards for peer reviewers (e.g., confidentiality, competing interests, timeliness, objectivity, acknowledgement of sources, confidentiality of manuscripts, and how to handle suspected misconduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation between research institutions and journals on research integrity cases: guidance from the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary — Institutions and journals both have important duties relating to research and publication misconduct. Instit…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Ethical oversight. Action: View web version; Download PDF (PDF, 178 KB). Guidance on roles and responsibilities of institutions and journals during investigations of research misconduct, recommended lines of communication, timelines, and confidentiality considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for retracting articles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Post-publication discussions and corrections. Action: Download PDF (PDF, 121 KB. Version 1, September 2009). Provides standards for when and how to retract or correct the published record, wording of notices, and distinctions between retractions, corrections, and expressions of concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for the Board of Directors of Learned Society Journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for the Board of Directors of Learned Society Journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Journal management. Action: Download PDF (PDF, 66 KB. Version 1, October 2008). Advises boards on governance, editorial independence, conflict-of-interest management, and strategic oversight of society journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to handle authorship disputes: a guide for new researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: By Tim Albert and Liz Wager — This document aims to help new researchers prevent and resolve authorship problems. In particular it provides: suggestions for good authorship practice that should reduce the incidence of such dilemmas, advice on what to do when authorship problems do arise, and a glossary of key concepts in authorship, with some reading lis…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action: Download PDF. Practical advice for researchers on authorship criteria, prevention of disputes, resolution pathways, and recommended communications with co-authors and institutions.
